samples.summary: hunt-ui.mjs re-implements seven CLI/orchestration helpers verbatim from hunt.mjs instead of reusing them
samples.evidence: `parseArgs`, `fail`, `strArg`, `repoSlug`, `gitSha`, `makeChangedSince` and `loadContext` in hunt-ui.mjs are near-identical copies of hunt.mjs:541-613 and hunt.mjs:1268-1302 (same `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq` invocation, same `git log --oneline sha..HEAD -- globs` conservative-false fallback, same deferrals/issues-corpus fallback and WARNING wording). The design doc's Phase 31 section explicitly reasons about what is shared and what is not — it justifies sharing `isFilingVerdict` and duplicating only the *report renderer* ('presentation: duplicating it costs a little prose and no correctness') — and says nothing about duplicating the issue-corpus loader or the git/ledger-expiry helpers, which carry real logic (corpus-unavailable degradation, ledger expiry). These are unexported module-private functions in the same directory; exporting them (as hunt-gate.mjs's helpers already are) would have been the repo's stated reuse posture. A change to corpus handling or slug resolution must now be made twice or silently diverge.

samples.summary: Renumbering UI Issue Hunting from Phase 28 to Phase 31 leaves a dangling cross-reference that now points at an unrelated phase
samples.evidence: The diff moves the 'UI Issue Hunting' section out of its (colliding) Phase 28 slot and re-adds it as '### Phase 31: UI Issue Hunting' (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1873), but docs/tasks/active/20260729-autonomous-issue-hunting-todo.md:89-91 still says 'moved to Phase 28 ... see docs/design/harness-engineering.md (Phase 28)'. Phase 28 in the doc is now '### Phase 28: Structured Rebuttal + Independent Adjudicator' (harness-engineering.md:1439), so the pointer resolves to the wrong section. The same task doc is also the PR ledger for this workstream (it lists PR 1/PR 2 but not PR 3/PR 4a).

samples.summary: New direct import edge from a packages/frontend script into scripts/agent/* crosses the seam the design doc describes as subprocess/artifact-only
samples.evidence: `checkPredictionFunnel` and `checkSeededFaultInServeMode` do `await import(`${repoRoot}/scripts/agent/hunt-ui-probe.mjs`)`, `hunt-ui-expect.mjs` and `hunt-ui-session.mjs`. The Phase 31 design text justifies the driver being a *subprocess* precisely because `scripts/agent` and `packages/frontend` are separate installs, and the workstream's own notes record the seam as 'a JSON artifact, not an import' (docs/tasks/active/20260729-autonomous-issue-hunting-todo.md:78-80). The direction is reversed here (frontend → scripts/agent) and works today only because those three modules happen to static-import nothing outside `node:`; nothing pins that property from this side, and the new coupling is only implied, not stated, in the design doc.

samples.summary: Stated wall-clock budget (~30 minutes) is inconsistent with the shipped persona config (4 serial briefs × 900s action budget + verification)
samples.evidence: The command file budgets '~$15 and ~30 minutes for 2 personas × 2 briefs (4 explorer sessions at maxActions: 80, plus up to 4 verified candidates × 2 verifiers per persona)', while scripts/agent/charters-ui/personas.json sets `actionBudget.totalTimeoutMs: 900000` (15 min) per brief and hunt-ui.mjs runs briefs SERIALLY, plus per-candidate replay (4 attempts × ~6s browser boot each) and verifier turns. Worst case is well over an hour. Since the number is the input to a mandatory human spend gate (step 3), an under-stated ceiling is the wrong direction to be wrong in.

samples.summary: Phase 31 records the orchestrator and the seeded control but not the new local front door or the `--fault` flag on the production `run` command
samples.evidence: Phase 26 documents `.claude/commands/hunt.md` as the 'Local front door' (harness-engineering.md:1244), but the Phase 31 status paragraph lists only 'the orchestrator, personas and the seeded control' and never mentions the new `.claude/commands/hunt-ui.md` playbook, nor that `hunt-ui.mjs run` itself accepts `--fault` (a mode that fabricates findings and suppresses the ledger write). The doc describes the seeded control only as something `verify:hunt:oracles` exercises, so a reader of the design doc would not know a fabricating run mode exists on the production entry point.

samples.summary: validatePersona does not require docsScope, yet both shipped rubrics offer ground B bounded by docsScope
samples.evidence: `validatePersona` checks id, surface, briefs, oracles, codeScope, reportableSeverities and verifiers, but never `docsScope`. Both rubrics (charters-ui/doc-writer.md and sheet-author.md) tell the explorer that ground B requires a `file.md:line` 'inside this persona's docs scope', and hunt.mjs's `validateCharter` pairs the two ('requiresDocCitation with no docsScope[] — nothing could ever pass', hunt.mjs:125-126). A persona shipped without `docsScope` would make ground B permanently ineligible and silently narrow what the hunter can report — the exact 'looks like it found nothing' failure the loud-validation design exists to prevent.
searchedFor: grep docsScope in scripts/agent (hunt.mjs:125, personas.json, hunt-gate.mjs)

verdict.reason: Verified in-tree. hunt-ui.mjs:655-717 defines parseArgs/fail/strArg/gitSha/repoSlug/makeChangedSince that are near-identical to hunt.mjs:541-613 — repoSlug uses the same `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner` call with the same null fallback, and makeChangedSince is byte-comparable including its `/** ... Drives ledger expiry. */` docblock and the conservative `return false` catch. hunt-ui.mjs:719-748 duplicates hunt.mjs:1268-1302's loadContext, including the identical "issue corpus unavailable … Duplicate suppression is WEAKER this run" warning wording (only the cfg fields differ; the underlying fetchIssues/renderIssues ARE shared via hunt-corpus.mjs, so the duplication is the composition + degradation path, a mild overstatement in the finding but not a refutation). The reuse reasoning the finding cites is real, though it lives in the file header at hunt-ui.mjs:14-29 (exact quoted phrase at line 24) with the parallel argument at docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1992-2001; both justify sharing isFilingVerdict and duplicating only the report renderer, and neither covers the corpus loader or the git/ledger-expiry helpers. The repo's stated posture is extraction — hunt-gate.mjs, hunt-corpus.mjs, hunt-probe.mjs, hunt-fingerprint.mjs and git-env.mjs are all imported as shared modules at hunt-ui.mjs:47-65 — so these duplicates are the outlier. Duplication/reuse is squarely in this lens's lane; no guard or existing shared module removes it.
